title: The seven practices and their purposes
blurb: Recall the purpose of each of the seven practices and match a project question to the practice that answers it.
question: A team wants a clear rule for when a forecast deviation must go to the project board as an exception. Which practice has the purpose of controlling deviations that cause an exception?

teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile keeps the seven PRINCE2 practices: business case, organization, plans, quality, risk, issues and progress. Each one keeps its PRINCE2 purpose. What changes in an agile project is how the practice is carried out: which management products are kept, tailored or replaced with agile artifacts, and which agile techniques support it. Learn the purposes first, because exam questions often describe a purpose and ask which practice it belongs to.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.1 to 12.1; Table 5.2

teach.caption: Big Owls Prefer Quiet Rivers In Parks. Chapters 6 to 12 of the book follow this order.

head: Practice
Its purpose
rows: Judge whether the project is, and stays, desirable, viable and achievable
Set up the structure of accountability and responsibilities (the who)
Define the products (what) and the means (who, how, where, when, how much)
Document users' requirements of the products and how they will be met
Identify, assess and control uncertainties affecting objectives
Collect and assess issues and control changes to the baseline
Compare actual with planned, forecast, control deviations causing an exception
teach.caption: Book sections 6.1, 7.1, 8.1, 9.1, 10.1, 11.1 and 12.1.

head: Practice
Question it helps answer
rows: Why does the project exist, and what must it stay aligned to?
Who is accountable and who is responsible? (hook)
What will we deliver, how, when and for how much? (hook)
What is acceptable to users, and how is it measured?
What if something unexpected happens, and how do we respond?
What now, when a product deviates from what was agreed?
Are we on track, and should we carry on? (hook)
teach.caption: Rows without '(hook)' follow Table 5.2. Hooks are our memory aids built from the purposes.

teach.h: Risk, issues and progress: the near misses
Which practice does this belong to?

root.label: Something is off track
root.sub: Ask what kind of thing it is

teach.body: In an agile project the purposes stay the same but the tools change. The business case is tailored to a project canvas, plans use a release map and backlogs, quality uses Definitions of Ready and Done, risk adds the Agilometer, issues are handled at the lowest sensible level, and progress is shown on team and project dashboards and burn charts.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 5.2; chapters 6 to 12

teach.body: Brackenford Council is building a digital parking-permit service. Project manager Tomasz Wilk sorts points from a progress review. 'Are residents still going to save time, and is it still worth doing?' is business case. 'Who decides on priorities across the two teams?' is organization. 'The payment supplier may go bust' is risk. 'Users asked for a new visitor-permit feature' is issues. 'We forecast missing the stage end date' is progress, because it is a deviation that could cause an exception.

teach.text: Do not mix up issues and progress. Issues controls CHANGES TO THE BASELINE; progress controls DEVIATIONS THAT CAUSE AN EXCEPTION. Also, V2 has no 'change theme': the old change theme is now the issues practice, and all seven are 'practices', not 'themes'.

items: Seven practices: business case, organization, plans, quality, risk, issues, progress.
Business case: desirable, viable and achievable, now and later.
Organization: the who. Plans: what, who, how, where, when, how much, for the why.
Quality: users' requirements and how they will be met.
Risk: control uncertainties. Issues: control changes to the baseline.
Progress: compare actual with planned, forecast, control deviations causing an exception.

summary: You can now recall the purpose of all seven practices in PRINCE2 Agile. You can also match a question or situation to the right practice, including the risk, issues and progress near misses.

A.q: Which practice has the purpose of defining and establishing the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities?
A.why: The organization practice defines and establishes the structure of accountability and responsibilities, the 'who' (7.1).

whyNot.1: Plans defines the products and the means to deliver them; the 'who' in plans is about resources for the work, not the accountability structure.
whyNot.2: Progress monitors actual against planned and controls deviations.
whyNot.3: Business case judges whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable.

A.q: Which is a purpose of the quality practice?
options: To control changes to the project's baseline
To identify, assess and control project uncertainties
To document the users' requirements of the products
To compare actual achievements with those planned
A.why: The quality practice documents the users' requirements of the project products and establishes the means by which they will be met (9.1).

whyNot.0: Controlling changes to the baseline is the issues practice (11.1).
whyNot.1: Controlling uncertainties is the risk practice (10.1).
whyNot.3: Comparing actual with planned is the progress practice (12.1).

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The purpose of the [?] practice is to collect and assess issues and to control changes to the project's baseline.
A.why: Collecting and assessing issues and controlling changes to the baseline is the purpose of the issues practice (11.1).

whyNot.0: Risk controls uncertainties that would affect objectives.
whyNot.1: Quality documents users' requirements and how they will be met.
whyNot.2: Progress controls deviations that cause an exception, not changes to the baseline.

B.q: Which practice is described as establishing mechanisms to judge whether the project is, and remains, desirable, viable and achievable?
B.why: That is the purpose of the business case practice, supporting decisions on continued investment (6.1).

whyNot.0: Plans defines what will be delivered and the means to deliver it, to satisfy the business case.
whyNot.2: Risk controls uncertainties; it supports, but does not judge, overall justification.
whyNot.3: Organization sets up accountability and responsibilities.

B.q:
Which two statements about the purposes of the practices are correct?
1. The progress practice provides a forecast for the project's objectives and continued viability.
2. The risk practice controls changes to the project's baseline.
3. The plans practice defines the products and the means to deliver them.
4. The organization practice judges whether the project is achievable.
B.why: Progress provides a forecast for objectives and continued viability (12.1), and plans defines the products and the means to deliver them (8.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: controlling changes to the baseline is the issues practice.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: baseline changes belong to issues, and judging achievability belongs to business case.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: judging achievability is the business case practice.

B.q: Which practice answers the question 'What if something unexpected happens, and how should we plan responses to it?'
B.why: Table 5.2 links that question to the risk practice, which identifies, assesses and controls uncertainties (10.1).

whyNot.0: Issues answers 'what now, when a product deviates from what was agreed?'.
whyNot.1: Progress compares actual with planned and controls deviations causing an exception.
whyNot.3: Quality answers 'what is acceptable to users and how is it measured?'.

C.q: A team forecasts that the stage will finish two weeks late, beyond the agreed time tolerance. Which practice's purpose covers controlling this, and what is being controlled?
options: Issues, because it controls changes to the baseline
Risk, because it controls uncertainties to objectives
Plans, because it defines when products are delivered
Progress, as it controls deviations causing exceptions
C.why: A forecast beyond tolerance is a deviation that causes an exception; controlling it is part of the progress practice's purpose (12.1).

whyNot.0: The issues practice controls changes to the baseline; a forecast breach of tolerance is handled by progress.
whyNot.1: Risk deals with uncertain future events, not a forecast breach of agreed tolerance.
whyNot.2: Plans sets out when products will be delivered, but controlling deviations is progress.

C.q: Which statement about the practices in PRINCE2 Agile is correct?
options: Each practice keeps its PRINCE2 purpose but is applied in an agile way
The issues practice is renamed the change practice in agile projects
Agile projects use five practices, dropping risk and progress
Each practice is replaced by an agile framework such as Scrum
C.why: PRINCE2 Agile keeps all seven practices and their purposes, and shows which products to keep, tailor or replace and which agile techniques help (Table 5.2).

whyNot.1: V2 uses 'issues'; 'change' was the name of the old theme.
whyNot.2: All seven practices apply; risk and progress are not dropped.
whyNot.3: Agile frameworks support delivery; they do not replace the practices.

C.q: A user asks for an extra language version of an approved feature, and separately the team lead fears a key developer may leave next month. Which practices handle each?
options: Risk for the request; issues for the developer
Issues for the request; risk for the developer
Quality for the request; progress for the developer
Progress for the request; organization for the developer
C.why: A request for change is an issue (issues controls changes to the baseline); a possible future event such as a developer leaving is a risk (an uncertainty).

whyNot.0: This reverses them: the request has already arisen, while the departure is uncertain.
whyNot.2: A change request is an issue; a possible departure is a risk, not a progress matter.
whyNot.3: Progress controls deviations from plan; a new request is an issue.

reteach.title: Seven questions every project keeps asking
reteach.question: If a project were a car journey, which practice would be the satnav's 'you are running late' warning?

blocks.body: The business case is why you are going at all. Organization is who drives and who navigates. Plans is the route and timings. Quality is what counts as arriving in good shape. Risk is the chance of roadworks. Issues is the passenger asking for a detour. Progress is the satnav comparing where you are with where you should be and warning when you will be late.

blocks.text: The detour request (issues) and the late warning (progress) feel similar. One is a change to the agreed route; the other is a deviation from plan that may need escalating.

explain.body: Business case judges whether the project is, and stays, desirable, viable and achievable. Organization sets the structure of accountability and responsibilities: the who.

test.q: Which practice's purpose supports decision-making about continued investment in the project?
test.why: The business case practice judges whether the project is and remains desirable, viable and achievable, supporting decisions on continued investment (6.1).

whyNot.1: Quality covers users' requirements and how they will be met.
whyNot.3: Plans defines products and the means to deliver them.

explain.body: Plans defines the products to deliver (what) and the means (who, how, where, when, how much) to satisfy the business case (why). Quality documents users' requirements of those products and how they will be met.

test.q: Which practice defines the 'what', 'who', 'how', 'where', 'when' and 'how much' to satisfy the 'why'?
test.why: That is the purpose of the plans practice (8.1).

whyNot.1: Progress compares actual achievements with plans; it does not create them.
whyNot.2: Organization covers accountability, not products and schedules.
whyNot.3: The business case is the 'why' that plans aim to satisfy.

explain.body: Risk identifies, assesses and controls uncertainties that would affect objectives. Issues collects and assesses issues and controls changes to the project's baseline.

test.q: Which practice controls changes to the project's baseline?
test.why: Controlling changes to the baseline is part of the issues practice's purpose (11.1).

whyNot.0: Risk controls uncertainties, not changes to the baseline.
whyNot.1: Quality defines requirements and how they will be met.
whyNot.2: Progress controls deviations that cause an exception.

explain.body: Progress monitors and compares actual achievements against those planned, provides a forecast for objectives and continued viability, and controls any deviations that cause an exception.

test.q: Which is a purpose of the progress practice?
options: To document the users' requirements of the products
To provide a forecast for objectives and viability
To set up the structure of accountability
To control changes to the project's baseline
test.why: Progress provides a forecast for the project's objectives and continued viability (12.1).
